# Testament of Naphtali — 8
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source Manuscript:** Greek MS (Codex Cantabrigiensis) | **Section:** Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs

---

**1:1** The copy of the testament of Naphtali, which he ordained at the time of his death in the hundred and thirty-second year of his life.
**1:2** When his sons were gathered together in the seventh month, on the first day of the month, while still in good health, he made them a feast and drank wine.
**1:3** And after he was awake in the morning he said to them: I am dying. And they believed him not.
**1:4** And as he blessed the Lord, he grew strong and said that after yesterday's feast he would die.
**1:5** And he began then to say: Hear me, my children, hear Naphtali your father.

**2:1** I was born from Bilhah; and because Rachel dealt cunningly, and gave Bilhah in place of herself to Jacob, and she conceived and bore me upon Rachel's knees, therefore she called my name Naphtali.
**2:2** For Rachel loved me very much, because I was born upon her lap; and when I was still tender she would kiss me, saying: May I have a brother of thine from mine own womb, like unto thee.
**2:3** Whence also Joseph was like unto me in all things, according to the prayers of Rachel.
**2:4** Now my mother was Bilhah, daughter of Rotheus the brother of Deborah, Rebecca's nurse, who was born on one and the same day with Rachel.
**2:5** And Rotheus was of the family of Abraham, a Chaldean, God-fearing, free-born and noble; and he was taken captive and bought by Laban; and he gave him Euna his handmaid to wife, and she bore Bilhah and Zilpah to him.

**3:1** And God made all things good in their order: the five senses in the head, and he added thereunto the neck, the hair also for comeliness and glory, the heart moreover for understanding, the belly for excretion, the windpipe for health, the liver for wrath, the gall for bitterness, the spleen for laughter, the reins for prudence, the loins for power, the backbone for fortitude.
**3:2** So then understand all things in order, and know that as the Lord made the body a type of the spirit, so also he made the spirit after the type of the body.
**3:3** For in the like manner as the senses of the body work together with each other, so also do the senses of the soul work one with another.

**4:1** Therefore understand all things in order, my children, and give diligence in all your doings to be orderly and proper before all men; and whatsoever the Lord commands in the order of his will, do ye in due order, and nothing out of season.
**4:2** For if thou tell the sun to go faster, it will not obey thee; neither will it cease shining if thou command it; for it abides in the order God created it.
**4:3** And so the moon and the stars do not change their order.
**4:4** So also ye: do not change the law of God in the disorderliness of your doings.

**5:1** And I tell you now, my children, of a vision which I saw in my life.
**5:2** Twelve deer were feeding; and the nine of them were divided and scattered over all the earth, and likewise the three.
**5:3** And I saw that from Judah was born a virgin wearing a linen garment; and from her went forth a Lamb, without spot; and on his left hand there was as it were a lion, and all the beasts rushed against him, and the Lamb overcame them and destroyed them and trod them under foot.
**5:4** And on account of him the angels and men rejoiced, and all the land.
**5:5** And these things shall come to pass in their season in the last days.
**5:6** Do ye therefore, my children, also keep all the commandments of the Lord; for there is hope for all who hold fast his way.

**6:1** And after he had said these things to them, he charged them to carry his bones up to Hebron and bury them there with his fathers.
**6:2** And while he was eating and drinking in much gladness, he covered his face and died.
**6:3** And his sons did as he had commanded them, and they carried him up to Hebron and buried him there with his fathers.

---
*End of Testament of Naphtali*
